args.plan_summary: Build a Flask admin management system with user authentication: login/logout/registration, role-based access (admin vs user), an admin dashboard with user CRUD, secure password hashing, CSRF protection, and a clean Bootstrap-based UI. Delegate research first, then implementation.

todos.content: Research current Flask auth best practices: Flask-Login + Flask-SQLAlchemy + Flask-WTF patterns, password hashing (Werkzeug), session/CSRF security, role-based access control, and latest stable package versions.
Scaffold project structure: config.py, run.py, requirements.txt, .env.example, README.md, and package layout (app/ with models, auth, admin, templates, static).
Implement app factory and extension setup: SQLAlchemy, Flask-Login, CSRFProtect, Bootstrap, CLI commands to init DB and create initial admin user.
Implement User model (id, username, email, password_hash, role, timestamps) with Werkzeug password hashing helpers.
Implement auth blueprint: register, login, logout, change_password with Flask-WTF forms and flash messages.
Implement admin blueprint: dashboard, user list, create/edit/delete user, role management, protected by login_required + admin_required decorators.
Create templates (base, auth pages, admin dashboard, user management) with Bootstrap styling and CSRF token in all forms; add static CSS.
Write smoke/flow tests with Flask test client: login flow, protected-route redirect, admin-only access control, password hashing check.
Run verification commands (install deps, init DB, run tests, start server) and fix any issues found.

acceptance_criteria: python run.py starts the Flask app without errors.
A fresh SQLite database is created and tables initialized; an initial admin user can be created via CLI.
Unauthenticated users are redirected to the login page for protected routes.
Login with correct credentials succeeds; wrong credentials are rejected with an error message.
Admin-only routes (user management, role changes, deletions) are denied to non-admin users (403 or redirect).
Passwords are stored only as hashes (Werkzeug scrypt/pbkdf2), never plaintext.
CSRF protection is enabled on all POST forms.
Registration creates a new user with the default 'user' role.
Admin dashboard shows user statistics and a user management table.
Automated smoke tests pass (login flow, access control, hashing).
verification_commands: python run.py --help  # CLI shows init-db and create-admin commands
python -m pytest -q  # runs tests/test_app.py smoke tests
.venv/bin/python -c "import run; app=run.create_app(); print(app.url_map)"  # sanity import/route dump

args.instruction: Research current best practices (2023-2025) for building a Flask admin/management system with user authentication. I need concrete, up-to-date guidance on: (1) the recommended Flask version and companion extensions (Flask-Login, Flask-SQLAlchemy, Flask-WTF, Flask-Bootstrap vs Bootstrap-Flask vs plain Bootstrap CDN) and their current stable versions; (2) secure password hashing in Flask/Werkzeug - what is the current recommended hash method (scrypt vs pbkdf2) and how generate_password_hash/check_password_hash are used; (3) CSRF protection best practice with Flask-WTF/CSRFProtect and how to handle the CSRF token in template forms and fetch/axios calls; (4) Flask-Login setup patterns: login_manager.user_loader, login_required, current_user, user roles and the recommended way to implement role-based access control (custom decorator vs flask-principal); (5) session security settings in Flask config (SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE, PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME, SECRET_KEY handling via env vars); (6) Flask app factory pattern with blueprints and CLI commands (flask --app, click commands like init-db, create-admin); (7) SQLAlchemy model patterns for a User model (password_hash column, timestamps, unique constraints). Save the findings and any authoritative source links (Flask docs, Flask-Login docs, Werkzeug docs, real-world examples) into research notes.
